title: Bulk Rollout Edit surface — hover, focus, and accessibility redlines
creator: Maya Nguyen
description:
Purpose: Finalize the visual and interaction spec for the bulk-edit surface on the Rollouts list and timeline. This ticket captures visual redlines, accessibility fixes, and edge-case microcopy so engineering can implement a keyboard-first, low-friction bulk-edit flow. Scope includes: selection UX (click, shift+click, keyboard), hover and focus states for compact items, bulk action confirmation microcopy, and error/failure state presentation for partially-applied changes. We are explicitly avoiding layout changes to the main timeline; this is a surface-level polish focused on states, animations, and a11y fixes.

Design goals:
- Make bulk-edit discoverable without adding new persistent chrome.
- Ensure focus/hover states have sufficient contrast and clear hit targets for high density lists.
- Provide safe defaults for destructive bulk actions and clear recovery paths for partial failures.

Trade-offs considered:
- Compact vs. spacious spacing: chose a slightly larger hit area (+6px) to improve keyboard navigation while keeping density acceptable for power users.
- Animation smoothing: limited to 80ms fade/slide to avoid distraction during large selections.
- Confirmation modality: opted for inline dismissible banner for small batches (<5) and modal confirmation for larger batches to reduce modal friction while protecting from accidental mass changes.
acceptance_criteria: Hover state: 12% darker surface with 2px outline on focus, passes WCAG AA against adjacent text color
Keyboard nav: Tab sequence includes checkboxes then bulk action bar; arrow keys traverse items and shift+arrow extends selection
Bulk action bar: appears pinned to top of list when one or more items selected; contains label ({count} selected), primary action, and dismiss
Destructive action flow: for more than 5 items, show modal with clear count, example affected routes, and an undo banner with 15s timer
Failure states: partial failures surface an inline error card per failed item with one-click retry and link to rollout logs
Design tokens: spacing, color, and motion values documented in Figma file and annotated for engineers
